8.5a — Win, Lose & the Death Loop

Every fight ends one of two ways, and today both are real: the boss dies and the door opens... or YOU die at 90% and learn what your death loop actually costs. The endgame is where design promises get tested.

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — win. In BossManager.Die() (8.2a), the boss's last act opens the door — a UnityEvent, exactly the lever's machinery from 5.2a, fired by code instead of a keypress:

[SerializeField] private UnityEvent onBossDead;

private void Die()
{
    Debug.Log("BOSS DOWN");
    onBossDead.Invoke();
    Destroy(gameObject);
}

Wire the listener in the Inspector: the exit door's SetActive(false), or a lever-style animation. Notice the design decision you just made: the boss does not know what a door is. Cause and effect, separated by an event — the same abstraction, now on your boss's tombstone.

Step 2 — lose (you know this road). Player death is 2.2a's loop: ChangeHealth hits zero → LoadScene("Start"). But a boss-fight death has a NEW question: what happens to the boss's health? Run it: die, walk back, re-enter. The boss is at full health, because the boss lived in the scene you just reloaded. Was that a bug or a design? Argue both sides — arcade says full reset (the fight is the test); modern says checkpoint (the fight is a story). Your game is an arcade: embrace it.

Step 3 — the death audit, boss edition. The walk-back is the real cost of dying here. Time it: spawn → through your cave beats → arena door → first exchange. That number is the player's frustration bill every wipe. Over 60 seconds and the final fight punishes the player for reaching it. Fix options (pick one, defend it): a shortcut that opens when the player first SEES the boss door; a checkpoint trigger just outside the arena; or shorter cave beats — the 7.5a audit comes home.

Bug Hunt: The two-loop tangle

  1. You die mid-shockwave; the scene reloads; a wave spawns in the NEW scene. Why CANNOT that happen (what does Destroy do to scene objects — and what does DontDestroyOnLoad protect instead)?
  2. Die exactly as your swing connects — health 0 at the same frame as ChangeHealth(-1) on the boss. Who wins? What does the order of operations in that single frame decide, and why do games resolve deaths AFTER the frame?
  3. The boss dies while the player is mid-jump over a shockwave. The door opens, the wave still flies, and the level wants to celebrate. Should the remaining waves die with the boss? Wire it: Die() finds all Shockwaves and destroys them — which pattern from 5.2a (FindObjectsByType) does that reuse?
  4. Player HP reaches zero in the SAME tick the boss's does. LoadScene fires; onBossDead fires. What did the player see for one frame — and why does the answer decide the FIGHT's winner for the record?
Playtest ~15 min

Partner plays the fight. You watch for ONE thing per run:

  • Run 1 — did they read the telegraphs? (Count dodges that looked deliberate vs. lucky)
  • Run 2 — did the phase changes change their BEHAVIOR, or just the numbers on the bar?
  • Run 3 — the victory: did the open door tell them the game was over (or did they keep looking for trouble)?

Tinker: Endgame polish

  1. Apply one fix from the runs, then re-run the exact beat that revealed it.
  2. Write your endgame numbers in the repo (fights to first clear, seconds per fight): this is real 9.5a-style data and it belongs in a commit message.
  3. Commit + push: "8.5a: win/lose loops + death audit".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Fire a UnityEvent from code when the boss dies
  • Explain scene-local boss health as an arcade design decision
  • Run a death audit with a stopwatch and defend your fix choice
  • Read three playtests for telegraphs, phases, and the victory read
